text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) typically causes no symptoms at all, which is why doctors often call it a "silent killer". You can learn more about the condition directly from the CDC.

list.snippet: Asymptomatic nature: Most people with high blood pressure feel completely fine.
Hidden damage: The condition can quietly harm your heart, brain, and kidneys over time without any warning signs.
Only way to know: You must have your blood pressure measured with a cuff.

text_blocks.snippet: Rare Signs of a Sudden Spike
If your blood pressure rises to very high levels rapidly, you might notice subtle or temporary signs. According to the Cleveland Clinic, these can include:

list.snippet: Headaches: Throbbing pain, often felt in the morning.
Vision changes: Blurry vision or spots in your eyes.
Shortness of breath: Getting winded easily during light activity.

text_blocks.snippet: Signs of a Medical Emergency (Hypertensive Crisis)

Blood pressure readings above 180/120 mm Hg are dangerously high. If a high reading is paired with specific warning signs, it is a medical emergency. The American Heart Association advises you to seek emergency care immediately if you experience:

list.snippet: Numbness or weakness (especially on one side of the body)
